newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Daventree sells stake in Prague utility.
newsitem.headline: Daventree sells stake in Prague utility.

text.p: Cyprus-based Daventree Ltd has sold its 43.3 percent stake in the Prague-based regional heat and electrical utility Prazska Teplarenska a.s., a Daventree spokesman said on Friday.
"The sale (of the Teplarenska stake) has been realised," Marek Stransky, a Prague-based spokesman for the Daventree investment group told Reuters.

Stransky however declined comment on a report in the Czech daily Mlada Fronta Dnes which quoted a spokesman for the Czech power utility Elektrarny Opatovice as saying the shares were sold to Opatovice unit DEOP. Opatovice officials were not available for immediate comment.

Daventree is owned by U.S.-born investor Michael Dingman and Czech-born Viktor Kozeny, founder of the Harvard Group of Czech investment funds which have been transformed into industrial holding companies.
The group has quietly sold holdings in Czech companies acquired in highly-publicised transactions in 1995, including stakes in chemical companies Spolana a.s. and Fatra a.s.
Daventree still holds major stakes in the Czech ocean shipping company Ceska Namorni Plavba a.s., paper maker Sepap a.s., and oil explorer Moravske Naftove Doly.
Prazska Teplarenska shares opened 50 crowns lower at 958 on the Prague Stock Exchange on Friday, while shares of Elektrarny Opatovice were trading 178 crowns lower at 4,066.
